items.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024
items.q: if I was going to be a jazz player I’d want to play like Chet Baker or Don Fagerquist at that time, those were my idols in jazz.

ctx.x: Well like when I first got on Woody’s band he had two jazz players. One was Don Rader who we became like brothers and really good friends. He did the main jazz chair. And then I sat on the other end and there wasn’t much jazz and fortunately the jazz I had was in a Harmon mute in a mic and that was easy because I thought nobody can hear this. But you know all the time growing up through the school system there was always a good little jazz player and you know when it came to playing you know the other person would

play and not me. And finally I don’t know if you’ve ever heard of this trumpet player Louie Valizan. He was with Esquivel! for a long time, he was with Perez Prado playing the high notes. He was just far beyond his age when I used to work with him with a little Latin band. And he played like Dizzy, he played double C’s — this was when he was 20 and I was 17. And there were two of us, two trumpet players. And he’d say, “You play a solo.” And I’d say, “No,” you know not after what I was hearing from you. I’d be…
I have a quote here from this book about Woody Herman.
